explanation: Every basic rational graph is the curve 1/x stretched and shifted. h slides the vertical asymptote (where the denominator hits zero and y blows up) left or right, while k slides the whole curve up to set the horizontal asymptote y = k that the branches flatten toward. a stretches the branches and, when negative, flips them into the opposite quadrants. Watch the two dashed asymptote lines move with the sliders and notice the curve can never touch them.
bullets: Vertical asymptote at x = h: the denominator is zero, so y is undefined there.
Horizontal asymptote at y = k: the value a/(x−h) shrinks to 0 far out, leaving y → k.
Sign of a sets which pair of opposite quadrants (around the asymptote crossing) the branches sit in.
